claims.text: Atomically dispersed Pt on oxygen-vacancy-engineered ceria–zirconia will improve catalytic activity relative to conventional Pt nanoparticles on alumina.
Atomically dispersed Pt on oxygen-vacancy-engineered ceria–zirconia will improve catalyst durability relative to conventional Pt nanoparticles on alumina.
The proposed catalyst can achieve improved performance while using less platinum-group metal.
The proposed synthesis anchors Pt as isolated atoms on the ceria–zirconia support.
Oxygen vacancies in ceria–zirconia stabilize atomically dispersed Pt through strong metal–support interactions.
Engineered oxygen vacancies act as anchoring sites for individual Pt atoms.
Vacancy anchoring produces enhanced Pt dispersion.
Strong Pt–support interactions facilitate rapid redox reactions.
The single-atom configuration minimizes Pt sintering during operation and aging.
The single-atom configuration minimizes catalyst deactivation.
Improved Pt dispersion and resistance to sintering permit reduced platinum loading.
The experimental catalyst will have higher pollutant conversion efficiency than the conventional Pt nanoparticle catalyst.
The experimental catalyst will show less performance decay during aging despite having lower platinum content.
The predicted improvements will hold under high-temperature, cyclic-redox automotive exhaust conditions.
The benefits may diminish if the ceria–zirconia support loses structural integrity.
Extreme sulfur poisoning may diminish the catalyst's benefits.
Unusually low operating temperatures may diminish the catalyst's benefits.
Conversion and durability improvements depend on synthesis parameters and operating conditions.
An optimal oxygen-vacancy density is required to maximize catalyst performance.
